{
 "summary": "Findings (read-only review of diff.patch against channels.ts, preferences.ts, alerts.ts, delivery.ts, oncall-feed.ts, settings-page.ts; there are no tests and no build config in the directory, so nothing was executed):

1. Title: Channel allow-list duplicates the canonical CHANNELS tuple
Severity: P2
Location: preferences.ts:3 (used at preferences.ts:20); canonical source channels.ts:1
Failure: Single Source of Truth. `ALLOWED_CHANNELS` is a hand-copied `["email","sms","push"]` that duplicates `CHANNELS` in channels.ts:1. If someone adds a channel to `CHANNELS` (and so to the `Channel` type and to `addressFor`), the parser still rejects it with "Unknown alert channel" and users can never pick it in settings. The `readonly Channel[]` annotation only catches entries that are not valid channels. It does not catch a channel that is missing from the list.
Fix: Delete `ALLOWED_CHANNELS`. Import `CHANNELS` and look names up with `CHANNELS.find((c) => c === name)`, or use a type guard such as `(CHANNELS as readonly string[]).includes(name)`.

2. Title: Strategy interface, class and factory wrap one loop with one implementation
Severity: P2
Location: delivery.ts:14-16 (`DeliveryStrategy`), delivery.ts:19-34 (`FallbackDeliveryStrategy`), delivery.ts:36-38 (`createDeliveryStrategy`); alerts.ts:12-19
Failure: Premature Abstraction / Shallow Wrapper / Indirection Tax. There is one strategy and nothing in the project uses a second one. The factory only calls `new`, and alerts.ts builds the strategy itself inside its constructor, so the interface cannot even be used to swap in another implementation. The result is three exported symbols plus a private field and constructor body in place of one loop. A reader has to follow factory -> class -> method to find a for-loop.
Fix: Replace all three with one exported function `deliverInOrder(sender, contact, channels, text): Promise<DeliveryResult>`. Restore `AlertDispatcher`'s constructor to `private readonly sender: Sender` and call `deliverInOrder(this.sender, contact, channels, text)` from `dispatch`.

3. Title: The "never empty" channel list is a comment, not an enforced rule
Severity: P2
Location: preferences.ts:8-9 (`channels: readonly Channel[]` with the comment "Never empty"), preferences.ts:37 (`set` accepts any value), delivery.ts:24/32, oncall-feed.ts:7
Failure: Only `parseChannelOrder` (called from settings-page.ts:8) prevents an empty list. The type allows `[]` and `PreferenceStore.set` accepts it from any caller. With `[]`, `deliver` makes no attempt and returns `{deliveredBy: undefined, failures: []}`. The feed then shows a broken line ending in "tried " with nothing after it, and the alert is silently not sent. Today settings-page.ts is the only producer in the repo, so this is a latent hole in the rule rather than an observed bug. The rule belongs to the data and should be enforced where the data is defined, not by one caller.
Fix: Type the field as a non-empty tuple, `readonly [Channel, ...Channel[]]`, and have `parseChannelOrder` return that type. Every producer is then checked by the compiler and the empty case cannot happen downstream, so neither delivery nor the feed needs a branch for it.

4. Title: A send that hangs blocks fallback forever
Severity: P2 (UNVERIFIED)
Location: delivery.ts:26
Failure: The request is to deliver "on the first channel that works", but the next channel is only tried if `sender.send` rejects. If a channel provider hangs, `await` never settles: the alert is never delivered on a later channel and the on-call feed never gets a line. I could not check this because no concrete `Sender` exists in the project (channels.ts:10-12 is only an interface), so I do not know whether real senders apply their own timeouts.
Fix: Confirm whether the real senders guarantee that `send` settles within a bounded time. If they do not, add a per-attempt timeout around the call (for example with `AbortSignal.timeout`) and record a timeout as a failure entry.

5. Title: A missing-preferences error escapes the feed instead of being reported
Severity: P3
Location: alerts.ts:24 (`preferences.get` throws, preferences.ts:33); oncall-feed.ts:5
Failure: Delivery failures are now returned as data for the feed, but a user with no stored preferences still makes `dispatch` throw. `dispatchForFeed` therefore rejects and the feed shows no NOT DELIVERED line for that alert, even though it is exactly the "why was this alert late or missing" case the feature exists to explain. The old code behaved the same way; the new reporting path just does not cover it.
Fix: Either report this case through the result (for example as an undelivered result with a "no preferences" reason), or state explicitly that callers of `dispatchForFeed` own this error.

6. Title: No tests for the new behavior
Severity: P2
Location: delivery.ts:22-33, preferences.ts:15-26, oncall-feed.ts:4-10
Failure: The diff adds no tests. Nothing checks:
- that delivery stops at the first channel that succeeds and does not try later ones;
- that failures are recorded in the user's order;
- that the all-failed result is correct;
- that the parser rejects unknown names, repeats, and empty input, and normalizes case and whitespace;
- the wording of the two feed lines.
Any regression in the ordering or stopping logic, which is the core of the request, would go unnoticed.
Fix: Add tests against a fake `Sender` that fails on chosen channels, assert the `DeliveryResult` and the feed string, and add table tests for `parseChannelOrder`.

Not defects (checked): in the success path, `failures` is returned empty or with the earlier failures, as intended; `String(error)` covers values thrown that are not `Error`s; `toLowerCase` plus `trim` plus the empty-segment filter handle input like "Push, ,email" correctly; `addressFor` covers every channel.

No files were modified.",
 "files_modified": []
}

{
 "summary": "Findings: 8 actionable issues in diff.patch. The largest is structural: the access token is now stored in two places, and the store pushes it into the client. Two P2 behavior defects follow. A request that gets a 401 after a concurrent refresh has finished starts a second refresh. Any 400 from the token endpoint signs the user out. There are also P2 problems with failure handling and the lack of tests. No tests or call sites exist in the project. Nothing was run; every finding comes from reading the code.

1. Title: Access token copied into the client and pushed back by the store. Severity: P2. Location: api-client.ts:14,22,25-27,41; session-store.ts:1,17,21-24,38,47,52. Failure: Parallel State / Bidirectional Coupling. The token's real home is SessionStore.current.tokens.accessToken. The diff adds a second copy in ApiClient.accessToken. Every store mutation now has to sync it by hand through setAccessToken, and session-store.ts now imports ApiClient, so the two modules depend on each other. The store can hold only one client (`client` field, line 17). If a second ApiClient is built on the same store, it silently takes the first client's place. The first client then never hears about signOut, signIn or refresh, and keeps sending a stale or revoked bearer token. This also breaks the store's documented rule (line 14) that everything other than the sign-in screen only reads it. The pre-diff send() read the token from the store, and nothing in the feature needs the copy. Whether a second ApiClient is ever built on one store is UNVERIFIED (no construction sites exist in this directory), but the sync logic is debt either way. Fix: delete accessToken, setAccessToken, attach, the `client` field, the ApiClient import and the three `this.client?.setAccessToken` calls. In send(), read `this.store.get()?.tokens.accessToken` as before.

2. Title: A 401 that lands after another caller's refresh starts a second refresh. Severity: P2. Location: api-client.ts:33-35, 46-49. Failure: This breaks "concurrent callers share one refresh request". Sequence: request A sends token T1. Meanwhile caller B refreshes, the session gets T2, and the finally block clears `refreshing`. Then A's 401 for T1 arrives, and line 35 calls refresh() again, which sends a second POST /oauth/token. The more requests are in flight when a token expires, the more redundant refreshes go out. The extra refreshes also rotate the refresh token for no reason. Fix: remember the token or session each request was sent with. On a 401, refresh only if the store still holds that same token; if it has already changed, just retry with the current token.

3. Title: Every 400 or 401 from the token endpoint signs the user out. Severity: P2. Location: api-client.ts:62-64. Failure: The comment says the check is for invalid_grant, but the code tests only the status. RFC 6749 section 5.2 returns 400 for invalid_request, unsupported_grant_type, invalid_scope and others, and 401 for invalid_client. So a client bug or a server misconfiguration ends a valid session, and the user loses their sign-in. Fix: sign out only when the response body's `error` is "invalid_grant", and treat any other failure as a transient refresh error.

4. Title: A failed early refresh aborts a request whose token is still valid. Severity: P2. Location: api-client.ts:32. Failure: isExpiring() turns true 30 s before real expiry (session-store.ts:12,33). If the refresh in that window fails for a transient reason (5xx, network error, or a parse error from parseTokenPair), get() throws, even though sending with the current token would have worked. The early refresh is meant to be an optimization, but it now makes requests less reliable. Fix: catch the error from the early refresh and continue with the existing token, unless the token is actually past expiry or the session was signed out.

5. Title: Callers get a token-endpoint error instead of an error for the path they asked for. Severity: P3. Location: api-client.ts:65 with 32/35; message change at api-client.ts:9. Failure: When the refresh fails, get("/me") rejects with ApiError("/oauth/token", 401). A caller such as profile.ts:8 cannot tell a failed resource request from a failed refresh, and signed-out from transient. The diff also dropped "GET" from the error message, so a resource failure now reads "/me failed with status 500" with no method. Fix: give refresh failures their own error type (for example SessionExpiredError after signOut), and keep the method in ApiError's message (or add a method field), since the class now covers POST too.

6. Title: Dead fallback for expiresIn duplicates the parser's validation. Severity: P3. Location: api-client.ts:5,66-69. Failure: Dead Code Is Debt. parseTokenPair (tokens.ts:16-18) already throws unless expires_in is a finite positive number, so the `pair.expiresIn > 0 ? ... : DEFAULT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS` branch can never run. It also goes against tokens.ts:8-9 ("every field is checked here and nowhere else"). Fix: delete DEFAULT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS and pass `pair` straight to replaceTokens.

7. Title: An in-flight refresh from an earlier session is shared with the next session's callers. Severity: P3. Location: api-client.ts:46-49, 54. Failure: `refreshing` is not tied to a session. Suppose a refresh starts for session A, then the user signs out and signs in as B. B's 401 retry (line 35) joins A's refresh. replaceTokens drops A's tokens (session-store.ts:45), so B retries with the same rejected token and gets a second 401 without ever refreshing. If A's refresh fails, B's caller gets A's /oauth/token error instead. Fix: store the session the refresh started from next to the promise, and start a new refresh when store.get() is a different session.

8. Title: No tests for the new refresh behavior. Severity: P2. Location: api-client.ts:31-70, session-store.ts:30-48 (the project has no test files). Failure: None of the behaviors the request asks for are tested: early refresh inside the margin, one retry on 401, one POST shared by concurrent callers, sign-out on invalid_grant, and a sign-out or sign-in during a refresh winning over replaceTokens. The interleaving bugs in findings 2 and 7 are exactly the kind of regression such tests would catch. Fix: add tests with a fake HttpTransport and an injected clock that cover each of these behaviors, including the interleavings in findings 2 and 7.

UNVERIFIED (not a finding): the token request (api-client.ts:56-61) sends a JS object body with no Content-Type. RFC 6749 requires application/x-www-form-urlencoded. Whether HttpTransport encodes it correctly depends on the real transport, which is not in this directory (transport.ts only defines the interface).",
 "files_modified": []
}

{
 "summary": "Findings: renderFixedWidth only produces correct 36-character records when every input already happens to fit. Nothing pads or checks the account or the amount, so a short account or a large amount shifts or widens the record. There are also four structural or minor issues. I ran a probe with bun against the actual files: [{account "123456789012", -12345 cents}, {account "12345", 5 cents}, {account "123456789012", 1e15 cents}] gave lines of length 36, 29 and 39: "2026-01-05123456789012       -123.45", "2026-01-0512345          0.05", "2026-01-0512345678901210000000000000.00".

1. Title: Account field is not padded or checked to 12 characters, so later columns shift
Severity: P2
Location: export.ts:17 (types.ts:2)
Failure: The doc comment at export.ts:14 promises an account field of 12 characters, but the code inserts tx.account as is. Transaction.account is typed as a plain string; "twelve-digit" is only a JSDoc comment and nothing enforces it. Any account that is not exactly 12 characters moves the amount column. The probe's "12345" account gave a 29-character record. In CSV this was harmless; in a positional clearing-house file it means misread amounts and accounts.
Fix: Enforce the width at the fixed-width boundary. Throw a clear error when tx.account.length !== 12 (or is not /^\d{12}$/). Better still, validate it where Transaction values are built so the invariant lives at its source. Do not pad silently, because the field is an identifier.

2. Title: Amount longer than 14 characters overflows its field silently
Severity: P2
Location: export.ts:17, export.ts:21-25
Failure: padLeft only adds characters; it never rejects input that is already wider than the field. formatAmount(1e15) is "10000000000000.00" (17 characters), which gave a 39-character record with no error. A fixed-width consumer would truncate or misparse it. This needs amounts of at least 1e11 currency units (14 characters including the sign and decimals), so it is a boundary-validation gap rather than a common case. It still corrupts data silently instead of failing.
Fix: Throw when formatAmount(...).length > AMOUNT_WIDTH, then pad with padStart.

3. Title: Shallow Wrapper / reimplementation: padLeft duplicates String.prototype.padStart
Severity: P3
Location: export.ts:21-25 (called at export.ts:17)
Failure: padLeft(value, width, " ") does exactly what value.padStart(width, " ") does. padStart is already the idiom in format.ts:3-4, the module this change created. The `fill` parameter has one caller and always gets " " (Speculative Code), and the loop rebuilds the string on every iteration.
Fix: Delete padLeft and use formatAmount(tx.amountCents).padStart(AMOUNT_WIDTH) at export.ts:17. That also puts the width check from finding 2 in one place.

4. Title: Single Source of Truth: the record layout is split between a comment, one constant and two implicit widths
Severity: P3
Location: export.ts:6-7, export.ts:14, export.ts:17
Failure: Only the amount width has a constant (AMOUNT_WIDTH). The date width (10) and account width (12) exist only in the doc comment at :14, and :14 and :6 both restate 14. The comment is the only description of the full layout and is not checked against the code. That gap is how finding 1 got through.
Fix: Declare the layout once, for example `const LAYOUT = { date: 10, account: 12, amount: 14 } as const`. Have renderFixedWidth enforce or pad each field from it and remove the widths from the comment.

5. Title: Dead Code Is Debt: the formatDate re-export from export.ts has no consumers
Severity: P3
Location: export.ts:4
Failure: The only importer of formatDate from export.ts was summary.ts, and this same diff points it at ./format.ts (summary.ts:1). A grep of the project finds no other importer of `./export.ts`, so this compatibility re-export has no consumer. It leaves two public homes for formatDate, which defeats the purpose of moving it into its own module.
Fix: Delete export.ts:4.

6. Title: No tests for the new clearing-house export or the moved formatters
Severity: P2
Location: export.ts:15-19, format.ts:1-10 (no test files exist in the project)
Failure: renderFixedWidth is a new external-format contract, and nothing pins its 36-character record shape, the right-alignment of negative and small amounts ("0.05"), or the field order. Findings 1 and 2 would have been caught by one length assertion. renderCsv's output after the refactor is also unprotected.
Fix: Add a test for renderFixedWidth: an exact expected line for a typical row, every line exactly 36 characters, a negative amount, and rejection of a wrong-length account and an oversized amount. Add one exact-output test for renderCsv to protect the refactor.

Checked and not reported: formatDate moved to format.ts unchanged. formatAmount behaves the same as the old inline (amountCents / 100).toFixed(2), so CSV output is unchanged. summary.ts was updated correctly. The record separator ("\n" with no trailing newline) and the character encoding the clearing house expects are UNVERIFIED, because no clearing-house spec is in the project. Confirm them against the upload spec.",
 "files_modified": []
}

{
 "summary": "Findings: no P1 defects. The pagination loop (pagination.ts:15-24) is correct as written. It starts at the bare path, parses each page, stops on a null cursor, and URL-encodes the cursor into `?cursor=`. Both list paths have no query string of their own (directory.ts:15,19), so adding `?` is safe. orgReport (org-report.ts:5) keeps working: listProjects and listMembers still return Promise<T[]>, and dropping `async` cannot cause a synchronous throw because fetchAllPages is async.

1. Title: Undisclosed defense against repeated cursors that covers only part of the risk it names
Severity: P3
Location: pagination.ts:13, pagination.ts:19-21
Failure: Speculative Code. The task only says the service returns cursor-paginated pages. Nothing in the project (json-client.ts:1-5, the diff) shows the service can send a cursor it already sent. The comment just restates the general idea that a repeat "would loop forever" and gives no observed case. The guard also doesn't do what the comment claims. A faulty server that keeps sending new non-null cursors (for example, a counter that never ends) still loops forever. Only an exact repeat is caught. So the code adds a Set, a branch and an error path for a risk nobody has seen, and the protection is incomplete.
Fix: Delete `seenCursors` and its branch. That shrinks the loop to parse, push, return-or-advance. If unbounded loops are a real concern, state the evidence and replace the guard with one bound that covers every case (a maximum page count). A Set of seen cursors doesn't cover them all.

2. Title: No tests for the new pagination behavior
Severity: P2
Location: pagination.ts:11-33 (no test file in the project)
Failure: There are no tests for fetchAllPages, listProjects or listMembers. The behaviors the change exists for have nothing protecting them: combining items from several pages, stopping on `next_cursor: null`, encoding the cursor into `?cursor=`, and rejecting a malformed page (missing `items`, non-string cursor). A future change could break page combining (for example, a regression back to reading only the first page) and nothing would catch it.
Fix: Add one test file that drives listProjects/listMembers with a stub JsonClient serving 2-3 pages. Assert the combined result, the exact second-request URL (including a cursor that needs encoding, such as `a/b+c`), and one rejection for a malformed page.

3. Title: The wire format (`items`, `next_cursor`, `?cursor=`) is assumed, not verified
Severity: P3 (UNVERIFIED)
Location: pagination.ts:8-10, pagination.ts:22, pagination.ts:29
Failure: The doc comment states the service's response shape and the code depends on the field names `items` and `next_cursor` and the query parameter `cursor`. Nothing in this project defines or tests that contract (json-client.ts only states that `get` returns decoded JSON), and I had no way to call the real service. If the real names differ (for example `nextCursor`, or a `page_token` query parameter), every call either throws "page has no items array" or fetches the first page again. With the repeat guard, that second case fails on the second request.
Fix: Check the field and parameter names against the directory service's API docs or one real response before merging. Encode them in the test fixture from finding 2.

Checked with no defect found: error messages still identify the org, because `path` contains the encoded org. Item parse errors still come from parseProject/parseMember unchanged. Promise.all in orgReport is unaffected. Removing the per-function array checks is safe because parsePage now does that check.",
 "files_modified": []
}

 "summary": "Findings:

1. Title: Reject fields that exceed their fixed widths.
Severity: P2.
Location: export.ts:17; export.ts:21-24.
Failure: The exporter silently emits records longer than the declared 36 characters. Location: export.ts:15-18.
Failure: The supplied project contains no tests for the new export. No regression test protects its exact field offsets, amount alignment, record separators, or overflow rejection. The runtime probe already demonstrates width violations that such tests would catch.

{
 "summary": "Findings:

1. Title: FeatureGate is a pass-through wrapper, and it does not decouple the pages from FlagStore as its doc comment claims
Severity: P2
Location: feature-gate.ts:5-11 (doc comment at :3-4); used at checkout-page.ts:1,8 and search-page.ts:1,3
Failure: Shallow Wrapper / Indirection Tax. `isOn` only calls `this.flags.isEnabled` (feature-gate.ts:9) and adds nothing new. FeatureGate is a concrete class whose only constructor takes the concrete `FlagStore` (:6), so pages still depend on how flags are delivered, just one hop further away. The comment at :3-4 says the opposite. The private `flags` field also makes the type behave nominally: anything passed to a page must be a real FeatureGate wrapped around a real FlagStore. No caller can supply a lighter test double or another flag source unless it uses a cast. The class also renames `isEnabled` to `isOn`, so readers now have two words for the same question.
Fix: Delete feature-gate.ts and have the pages take a narrow structural type that FlagStore already meets, e.g. `type FeatureGate = Pick<FlagStore, "isEnabled">` or `interface FeatureGate { isEnabled(name: string, userId: string): boolean }`. Callers can then pass a FlagStore or a stub object directly, with no wrapper object and no second method name.

2. Title: Changing the page signatures breaks every caller that passes a FlagStore
Severity: P2 (whether this reaches real code is UNVERIFIED: no callers are in this snapshot)
Location: checkout-page.ts:8, search-page.ts:3
Failure: Both public functions now require a `FeatureGate`. Severity: P2
Location: api-client.ts:14,22,25-27,41; session-store.ts:1,17,21-24,38,47,52

The store holds a single `client` slot, so a second `new ApiClient(..., store, ...)` silently detaches the first one. The first client then keeps sending a stale token after any refresh or sign-in: 401, a wasted refresh, then a thrown 401. The original code read `this.store.get()?.tokens.accessToken` in `send` and had none of these problems. 2. Title: Requests that get a 401 after a refresh has finished start a second refresh instead of sharing it
Severity: P2
Location: api-client.ts:33-35 (with 46-50)
Failure: This breaks a stated requirement: "concurrent callers share one refresh request." Requests A and B go out at the same time with the same revoked token and both get 401. A calls `refresh()`; it completes and `finally` clears `refreshing`. B's 401 arrives later, so B finds `refreshing` undefined and issues a second POST /oauth/token, even though the token B sent has already been replaced. With N concurrent requests whose 401s arrive spread out, there can be up to N refreshes. If the server rotates refresh tokens with reuse detection, the extra exchanges also burn tokens for no reason. In the reverse case, a 401 for session S2 can join an in-flight refresh started for S1 (after a re-sign-in). That refresh is a no-op for S2 (replaceTokens drops it), and the retry fails.
Fix: Capture the session (or access token) used in `send`. On 401, refresh only if `this.store.get()` is still that session; otherwise retry right away with the current token. This makes refresh dedup depend on which token was rejected, not on timing.

3. Title: The fallback for `expiresIn` can never run
Severity: P3
Location: api-client.ts:5,66-69
Failure: Dead Code Is Debt. `parseTokenPair` already throws unless `expiresIn` is a finite number greater than 0 (tokens.ts:16-18). So `pair.expiresIn > 0 ? pair.expiresIn : DEFAULT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS` always takes the first branch, and `DEFAULT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS` is never used. It suggests a lenient contract that doesn't exist, and it repeats validation after the trusted boundary (tokens.ts:8-9: "checked here and nowhere else").
Fix: Delete the constant and call `this.store.replaceTokens(session, pair)`.

Severity: P3
Location: api-client.ts:62-64
Failure: The comment says the sign-out is for `invalid_grant` (a revoked refresh token). The code signs out on any 400 or 401 and never reads the error body. Under RFC 6749 §5.2, 400 also covers `invalid_request`, `unsupported_grant_type`, `invalid_scope`, and so on, and 401 is `invalid_client`. Those are client or configuration errors, not proof that the session can't recover. The code and its comment disagree. The ownership guard is also split: the `this.store.get() === session` check is done here for `signOut` but inside the store for `replaceTokens`.
Fix: Either check `body.error === "invalid_grant"` before signing out, or reword the comment to match the status-only rule. Consider `store.signOut(from: Session)` with the same guard as `replaceTokens`, so the "a newer session wins" rule has a single owner.

Severity: P3
Location: api-client.ts:32, 65, 9

 "summary": "Findings:

1. Title: Intent Drift: Do not shorten Retry-After to the backoff cap.
Severity: P1.
Location: retrying-transport.ts:79.
Failure: The request requires honoring Retry-After, but Math.min truncates the server's requested delay. A 503 with Retry-After: 120 causes another request after only 10 seconds under the default policy, rather than 120 seconds. A real local HTTP server through FetchTransport reproduced this with maxDelayMs=1000: the wrapper requested a 1000 ms sleep for Retry-After: 120. This retries during the server's requested waiting period and can exhaust all attempts before recovery. Retry-After specifies how long to wait before a follow-up request: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Retry-After.
Fix: Apply maxDelayMs only to exponential backoff. Honor valid server delays without shortening them; if the client cannot wait that long, return the response instead of retrying early. Update retrying-transport.test.ts:67-72, which currently asserts the conflicting behavior.

2. Title: Reject malformed Retry-After values before parsing them as dates.
Severity: P2.
Location: retrying-transport.ts:77-78.
Failure: Date.parse accepts strings that are not HTTP dates. Consequently, invalid delay values such as -1 and 1.5 are interpreted as old dates, become zero waits, and bypass exponential backoff. Both values reproduced a zero sleep through a real local HTTP server and FetchTransport; the configured fallback would have slept 50 ms. This contradicts the documented invalid-header fallback and makes malformed responses trigger immediate retries. Retry-After permits an HTTP date or nonnegative integer seconds: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Retry-After.
Fix: Recognize supported HTTP-date syntax before calling Date.parse; return undefined for other non-integer values so normal backoff applies. Extend the existing malformed-header test at retrying-transport.test.ts:88-93 with these cases.

Verification: bun test retrying-transport.test.ts passed all 11 tests and 19 assertions. Local HTTP probes confirmed both findings.
